summary: Register Qwen (Alibaba Cloud) as a further ai-family provider for the Task-122 AI provider account capability, reusing DashScope's OpenAI-compatible mode wire format without importing connectors/openai-compatible or connectors/kimi (provider packages may not import each other).

impacts.evidence: Qwen reuses the Task-122 ai_provider_accounts table and secret binding; it adds no tenant persistence of its own.
The only tenant text that leaves TORGNEXA through this provider is the caller-assembled analytics prompt at analyze-call time; no response is persisted by this package.
Qwen is reached through the existing Task-122 /settings/ai-providers:analyze operation; no new public operation is added, only the provider enum widened on already-additive schemas.
No EventBus schema is published or consumed.
Adds the qwen provider under the existing ai family/ai.completion.generate capability; dispatch by provider id is confined to internal/platform/builtinruntime.

Migration 000015 widens the ai_provider_accounts_provider_check CHECK constraint to admit 'qwen' and 'deepseek'; purely additive expand-phase change, verified applied against a live PostgreSQL 18 instance alongside the full 15-migration active chain.

Provider code has no direct network authority; all HTTPS calls are host-mediated through builtinruntime's DNS-pinned, public-IP-only transport. Credential bytes are read only inside a host-owned UseSecret callback.
Reuses the Task-122 ai.analyze / settings.ai_providers.* capability gates unchanged.
Reuses the Task-122 audit entries unchanged.
This capability performs no remote-state synchronization.

Outbound calls use a host-injected transport to a fixed default host (dashscope.aliyuncs.com) or an account-configured hostname override (for example the international DashScope region); no inbound webhook surface is added.
Remote non-2xx responses and empty/malformed completions normalize to a bounded error; the manifest's rate_limit/retry policy bounds concurrency and backoff.
Disabling the account row immediately stops further Qwen analyze calls; no other component depends on this provider.

Package tests cover the default-DashScope-host fallback, the compatible-mode path shape and a host override; the canonical Task-064 conformance suite passes all thirteen checks (docs/connectors/qwen/conformance-report.json), including sandbox_isolation verified under a privileged Linux runner.
